newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 oil demand up 2.8 pct from 1995 - API.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 oil demand up 2.8 pct from 1995 - API.

text.p: U.S. demand for petroleum products rose 2.8 percent in 1996 from the previous year, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
In its year end report, the API said deliveries of oil products, the key indicator of demand, were up 2.8 percent to average 18.21 million barrels per day.
It said petroleum imports jumped 6 percent in 1996 from 1995, the biggest year-to-year increase since 1993. U.S. dependency on oil imports amounted to 51 percent.
U.S. crude oil production fell for the fifth straight year, and averaged 6.45 million barrels per day, down 1.8 percent from 1995. Total imports averaged 9.36 million bpd in 1996, API said.
U.S. crude oil production fell for the fifth straight year, and averaged 6.45 million barrels per day, down 1.8 percent from 1995.
Production in the lower 48 states rose slightly in the last half of the year because of success of offshore development in the Gulf of Mexico, it said.
Oil demand was up mostly on increased use of distillate, jet fuel and liquefied petroleum gases. Gasoline deliveries rose slightly and residual fuel was down slightly.
With tight crude markets oil markets throughout the year, the API said stocks of crude oil and products were low compared with recent years.
In a breakdown of products, the report said gasoline deliveries were up 0.7 percent from 1995 and averaged 7.84 million bpd.

Reformulated gasoline increased market share in 1996 to 30 percent, up from 26 percent in 1995. RFG deliveries amounted to more than 2.3 million bpd, while oxygenated gasoline deliveries, which slipped, accounted for 400,000 bpd.
Distillate deliveries were up 4.7 percent, the highest level since 1979, and averaged 3.36 million bpd. Growth was concentrated in low-sulfur diesel fuel for highway use.
Kerosene jet fuel deliveries were up 6 percent, a record resulting from continued strength of commercial air traffic, and averaged 1.59 million bpd.
Residual deliveries dipped by 0.7 percent from 1995, and averaged 846,000 bpd.

Total inventories of crude and petroleum products were 932 million barrels at the end of 1996, about 40 million barrels lower than at the end of 1995, and about 100 million barrels lower than two years ago.
Refinery utilization for 1996 averaged 93.2 percent, the highest annual rate in at least 20 years. Distillate production rose by more than 5 percent to reach a record annual high of 3.32 million bpd.
